_comment: OPS-DEPLOY-INTERLOCK-CRON-DEFER-W1 — the DECLARED set of crons a deploy can decapitate. Read by ops/scripts/deploy-cron-interlock.sh (its only consumer) and asserted by scripts/check-cron-interlock-coverage.mjs. THE CLASSIFICATION IS THE DELIVERABLE; the dispatch code around it is small. Placement is DERIVED, not taste: check-declaration-coverage.mjs pins CONSUMER_DIRS = ['ops/monitoring','ops/cron'], so a declaration read only from ops/scripts/ has zero readers there and would sit half-declared; and it needs no sync because deploy.yml runs `git reset --hard origin/main` BEFORE it invokes the interlock, so this file is always current at the only moment it is ever read. (Correcting the dispatching spec's third reason: ops/scripts/ IS placed on the host by that same reset, but monitoring-inventory-reconcile.py's ORPHAN scan is scoped to MONITORING_DIR=/opt/algovault-monitoring and never sees it — the CONSUMER_DIRS leg is the load-bearing one.)

_classes.safe-to-kill: Atomic-replace publish, checkpoint-resumable, or idempotent on next fire. The deploy does NOTHING. The row exists so a future reader sees the job was CONSIDERED, not missed.
_classes.preempt-and-catchup: Killing loses work that a bounded catch-up can repair. SIGTERM, wait up to the derived budget for a checkpoint, then launch an SLO-gated catch-up detached.
_classes.no-safe-kill: Neither atomic nor repairable. Bounded wait, then PROCEED ANYWAY with a loud DEFERRED record. A deploy must never hang on a batch job.
_classes._indeterminate: A row whose `reason` is missing or empty is INDETERMINATE, never a silent safe-to-kill. Same convention as schedule-boundary-rule.json's exemptions.

_enumeration.command: crontab -l | grep -vE '^\s*(#|$)'   # then resolve each entry to its script and grep that script for a command-position `docker exec`
_enumeration.note: Rows are keyed by PROCESS PATTERN, not by cron line: the interlock matches patterns, and one pattern (seed-signals.js) covers 28 cron lines. `cron_lines` on each row records the fan-out so the enumeration stays recoverable. The prior enumeration measured 91 active lines (OPS-HOST-KERNEL-REBOOT-W2) and 75 before that (W1) — re-derive, never inherit.

_containers.evidence: deploy.yml runs `docker compose up -d --build --force-recreate` in /opt/crypto-quant-signal-mcp; docker-compose.yml declares services mcp-server, facilitator, postgres. The plausible-ce-* containers are a SEPARATE compose project and are not touched.
_containers.note: A `docker exec` into ANY of the three dies at that moment. `docker exec` into a non-signal-mcp container, and any host process, is out of scope by construction — see `exclusions`.

rows.reason: Checkpoints at a venue/group boundary and resumes from DB state, so a truncated run is safe — but 10 of 32 nightly runs (31.2%, 60d window, measured 2026-08-22) ended early, 10 of 10 attributed to a deploy, and the resulting lag can push a major venue past its 24h SLO. Preemption is kept because it costs zero deploy latency; the harm is REPAIRED afterwards by an SLO-gated catch-up rather than prevented.
rows.runtime_instrument: /var/log/carry-labeler.log — ISO-stamped lines grouped into runs on a 600s gap; max span over n=374 runs, read 2026-08-29
rows.cron: 23 2 * * * (via dist/scripts/nightly-carry-labeler.js, which spawns this as a child)
rows.notes: SEEDED FROM THE HARDCODED BEHAVIOUR WITH ZERO CHANGE. Every value here is what deploy-labeler-interlock.sh had inline: the same pattern, the same lock, the same catch-up argv, the same SLO gate. `pkill -0 -f 'dist/scripts/backfill-directional-labels'` verified live 2026-08-29 03:33Z (rc=0) against container PID 17365. Its PARENT nightly-carry-labeler.js is deliberately NOT the pattern — the child is the resumable half, and the parent dies with the container regardless.

rows.reason: It sends an on-chain Base-mainnet `publishRoot` transaction and THEN writes the batch row + per-signal proofs to Postgres. Measured 2026-08-29: tx confirmed 00:05:04.169Z, batch complete 00:05:07.639Z — a ~3.5s window in which a recreate leaves a Merkle root committed on chain with no database record of it. Re-running does not repair that: getNextBatchId() mints a NEW batch id, so the orphaned root is permanent. Not atomic, not resumable, not idempotent — the only row in this registry that is genuinely none of the three.
rows.runtime_instrument: /var/log/merkle-publish.log — ISO-stamped lines grouped into runs on a 600s gap; max span over n=7 runs, read 2026-08-29
rows.notes: THIS IS THE ROW THAT KEEPS THE 18:00-02:59 UTC WINDOW ALIVE AS A DECLARED CONTROL. It fires at 00:05 UTC, inside that window, which is very likely what the folklore was protecting without anyone having written it down. The whole job is ~7s, so a 120s bounded wait covers it comfortably — the deploy is delayed by at most one job length and then PROCEEDS regardless.

rows.reason: A 7h+ weekly LLM probe sweep with no checkpoint and no resume: a kill loses the whole week's GEO measurement, the next fire is 7 days away, and re-running costs real LLM spend for data that is dated to its run week. No bounded catch-up can repair it, and no bounded wait can outlast it — so the honest ruling is a loud DEFERRED and a deploy that proceeds anyway.
rows.runtime_instrument: /var/log/geo-weekly-cron.log mtime 2026-08-24T08:12:43Z minus its scheduled fire Mon 01:00:00Z = 26,363s; n=1 (the log carries no per-line timestamps, so only the most recent fire is derivable). Lower bound, not an average.
rows.notes: Its own log tail carries `[pg-pool] idle client error (recovering): terminating connection due to administrator command` — the signature of a Postgres bounce hitting it mid-run. It RECOVERED from that one and kept extracting, so the pool is resilient to a postgres recreate; the exposure is the mcp-server recreate, which kills the `docker exec` itself with nothing to recover. Also fires inside the 18:00-02:59 window.

rows.reason: Idempotent on next fire, and killing it is if anything corrective: every cron line is `flock -n`-guarded, so while one instance is stuck the next fire SKIPS rather than queues. A kill releases the lock and the following fire re-derives from live venue state. Nothing is lost that the next sweep does not recompute.
rows.runtime_instrument: host `ps -eo etimes,args`, n=32 samples @5s across two windows 2026-08-29 03:20Z/03:35Z, plus n=130 @1s; max observed lifetime of any single instance
rows.cron: 27 lines across timeframes 3m..1d x {HL, shadow, promoted} — see `_enumeration.command`
rows.notes: The single longest-lived non-labeler process measured on the box (2h19m). It is on this list because its LIFETIME makes a deploy collision near-certain, not because the collision is harmful.

rows.reason: Idempotent on next fire at a 3-minute cadence and `flock -n`-guarded. It backfills outcomes for signals that do not yet have them, driven entirely by DB state, so a truncated run leaves exactly the same work queued for the next fire ~3 minutes later.
rows.runtime_instrument: host `ps -eo etimes,args`, n=130 samples @1s, 2026-08-29 03:37Z; max observed instance lifetime
rows.notes: Runs far longer (13m) than its 3-minute cadence, so an instance is alive most of the time and a deploy nearly always kills one. Harmless by construction, and recorded so that is a finding rather than an assumption.

rows.reason: Backlog-driven and budgeted: it labels UNLABELED decisions from DB state under `--max-decisions 4000 --time-budget-min 90`, so it already terminates mid-backlog by design every night. A deploy-induced kill is indistinguishable from hitting the budget, and the remainder is picked up by the next nightly. Its `--check` pre-pass records the backlog size, so a growing queue is visible rather than silent.
rows.runtime_instrument: /var/log/hold-decision-labeler.log — ISO-stamped lines grouped into runs on a 600s gap; max span over n=2 runs, read 2026-08-29

rows.reason: Writes one hourly structural tuple per venue; a lost hour is repaired by the existing retro-basis-backfill host lane (OPS-BASIS-RETRO-BACKFILL-W1), which writes into the same oi_snapshots table. Idempotent on next fire for the following hour.
rows.runtime_instrument: /var/log/oi-sampler.log — ISO-stamped lines grouped into runs on a 600s gap; max span over n=2415 runs, read 2026-08-29

rows.reason: A kill costs at most one skipped post of one type. Each weekday fire publishes a DIFFERENT --type, so a truncated run is never re-attempted with the same payload and cannot double-post; the loss is one advisory dev.to item, and nothing downstream depends on its presence.
rows.runtime_instrument: /var/log/agent-forum.log mtime 2026-08-28T12:02:26Z minus its scheduled fire Fri 12:00:00Z = 146s; cross-checked against the same log's ISO-line run grouping (max span 21s over n=5 runs) — the mtime figure is the conservative one and is the one recorded

rows.reason: A read-mostly alert evaluation loop, idempotent on next fire: critical mode fires every 2 minutes and digest mode daily. A killed evaluation re-evaluates the same live state on the next tick; the only state it mutates is its own cooldown markers, which are re-derived.
rows.runtime_instrument: host `ps -eo etimes,args`, n=130 samples @1s spanning a full */2 fire cycle, 2026-08-29 03:37Z; max observed instance lifetime

rows.reason: A read-only coverage probe: one psql SELECT as aoe_readonly plus one in-container `node -e` that imports dist/lib/tf-support.js. It writes no application state, and the next hourly fire re-derives the same verdict from live data.
rows.runtime_instrument: /var/log/seed-coverage-canary.log mtime 2026-08-29T02:37:01Z minus its scheduled fire 02:37:00Z = 1s

rows.reason: Idempotent by construction — dwr_baseline_runs has PRIMARY KEY (run_month, spec), so a forced re-run refreshes the month rather than appending. Its own inventory row already records that it is safe to run by hand.
rows.runtime_instrument: /var/log/dwr-baseline-snapshot.log — its own `start` line 2026-08-24T07:56:01Z to log mtime 07:56:08Z = 7s; n=1 (the log retains one run)

rows.reason: A daily read-only report that ends in a Telegram digest send. A kill costs one skipped digest; the next fire re-derives it from live DB state and nothing consumes the missing one.
rows.runtime_instrument: /var/log/venue-readiness.log mtime 2026-08-28T06:05:04Z minus its scheduled fire 06:05:00Z = 4s

rows.reason: Read-only weekly digest over stored analytics. A kill costs one skipped digest and mutates nothing; the next fire recomputes from the same rows.
rows.runtime_instrument: /var/log/chat-analytics-digest.log mtime 2026-08-23T09:00:02Z minus its scheduled fire Sun 09:00:00Z = 2s

rows.reason: Read-only weekly rate-limit telemetry digest. A kill costs one skipped digest and mutates nothing.
rows.runtime_instrument: /var/log/shadow-digest.log mtime 2026-08-23T00:00:02Z minus its scheduled fire Sun 00:00:00Z = 2s

rows.reason: DETECT-only — it computes a payout digest and sends it; it moves no funds and writes no payout state, so a kill costs one skipped monthly notice. Recorded explicitly BECAUSE its name suggests otherwise and because it fires at 08:07 on the 1st, inside the measured peak deploy hour (T08 = 150 deploy events over 2026-07-28..08-26, measured by OPS-HOST-KERNEL-REBOOT-W3's `journalctl -u docker` sweep).
rows.runtime_instrument: /var/log/referral-payout.log mtime 2026-08-01T08:07:02Z minus its scheduled fire 08:07:00Z = 2s

rows.reason: Regenerates knowledge pages from the committed bundle; idempotent on next fire and the previous generation stays served until it succeeds.
rows.runtime_instrument: /var/log/refresh-knowledge-pages.log mtime 2026-08-23T06:00:02Z minus its scheduled fire Sun 06:00:00Z = 2s

rows.reason: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY is transactional: an interrupted refresh rolls back and the previous matview contents stay queryable. Idempotent on next fire 5 minutes later.
rows.runtime_instrument: host `ps -eo etimes,args`, n=20 samples @5s, 2026-08-29 03:20Z; max observed instance lifetime

rows.reason: An interrupted VACUUM (ANALYZE) leaves the table fully consistent — Postgres commits reclaimed space incrementally and abandons the rest. Idempotent on next fire, and autovacuum covers the interim.
rows.runtime_instrument: /var/log/oi-vacuum.log mtime 2026-08-01T04:00:02Z minus its scheduled fire 04:00:00Z = 2s

rows.reason: Diagnostic by design — no auto-install, no auto-copy, no mutation of anything it inspects. A kill costs one daily reconciliation; the next run re-derives every check from live host state.
rows.runtime_instrument: direct timed run on signal-1 under ALGOVAULT_TG_TEST_INERT=1, 2026-08-29 03:36Z (the slowest of the nine host-only docker-exec canaries measured the same way)

rows.reason: All eight are read-only probes that mutate no application state, and every one of them completed in 5 seconds or less when timed directly. Each re-derives its verdict from live state on its next fire, so a deploy-induced kill costs at most one skipped evaluation cycle. Grouped into one row because the class, the evidence and the ruling are identical for all eight; the `script` field enumerates them so none is hidden behind the grouping.
rows.runtime_instrument: direct timed runs on signal-1 under ALGOVAULT_TG_TEST_INERT=1, 2026-08-29 03:36Z: db-superuser 0s, directional-label-freshness 2s, outcome-backfill-freshness 0s, quota-exhaustion 0s, stripe-webhook-events 1s, tier-misclassification 5s, venue-slo-tiers-drift 1s, webhook-delivery 0s. Recorded value is the max.

exclusions.what: The 42 active cron lines on signal-1 that never reach a crypto-quant-signal-mcp-* container. 100 active lines, 46 with a direct `docker exec`, 12 more reaching one through a host script — 58 covered by `rows`, 42 excluded here.
exclusions.reason: `docker compose up -d --build --force-recreate` recreates only the three services in /opt/crypto-quant-signal-mcp/docker-compose.yml. A cron that runs as a host process, or execs into a container belonging to another compose project, is not reachable by this deploy at all — there is nothing for an interlock to protect. Excluded by construction, not by judgement.
exclusions.re_derivation_command: crontab -l | grep -vE '^\s*(#|$)' | grep -v 'docker exec'   # then, for each resolved script path, `grep -E '(^|[;&|]|\$\(|\bexec[[:space:]])[[:space:]]*docker[[:space:]]+exec' <script>` and confirm it is empty

exclusions.reason: OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS DEPLOY, settled by probe rather than by assumption. It belongs to the algovault-bot repo (absent from this one), and it runs a HOST process — `/opt/algovault-bot/.venv/bin/python scripts/entitlement-drain.py` — with zero `docker exec` anywhere in it. `docker compose up --force-recreate` on the signal-mcp stack cannot touch it.
exclusions.separate_finding: Its SCHEDULE is a different problem and is deliberately NOT fixed here: those ten minutes occupy every canonical off-boundary slot in the hour, which is why signal-1 has only :09 and :39 free and why OPS-HOST-AUTO-REBOOT-W1 faces a 2-minute target. Filed as OPS-BOT-CRON-SCHEDULE-GREED-W1; it is a bot-repo change and cannot ship from a signal-mcp wave. Note also that the script's own header docstring claims `*/5 * * * *`, which the live crontab contradicts — the docstring is stale and belongs to the same follow-up.

exclusions.reason: Both contain the literal string `docker exec`, and neither invokes it. One occurrence is a `#` comment recording a RETIRED implementation; the other sits inside an alert-body heredoc ('... host dist/ unusable AND docker exec failed ...'). A mention is not an invocation — the same rule check-canaries-wired.mjs already carries for comments and check-test-budget.mjs carries for string literals. scripts/check-cron-interlock-coverage.mjs therefore matches `docker exec` only in COMMAND POSITION, after stripping comments.
exclusions.re_derivation_command: sed -E 's/(^|[[:space:]])#.*$/\1/' ops/cron/<f>.sh | grep -cE '(^|[;&|]|\$\(|\bexec[[:space:]])[[:space:]]*(sudo[[:space:]]+)?docker[[:space:]]+exec\b'   # expect 0 for these two, 1..2 for the three real ones

_residual_no_safe_kill.ruling: The 18:00-02:59 UTC deploy-free window is NOT retired. It is now a DECLARED control with two named rows justifying it, both of which fire inside it (00:05 and Mon 01:00). What changes is that it stops being folklore carried by an agent-side memory file — a third rule source in an estate that declares two — and becomes data these rows own. OPS-HOST-AUTO-REBOOT-W1 should read this block, not the memory file.
_residual_no_safe_kill.retire_when: publish-merkle-batch writes its batch row in the same transaction boundary as (or before) its on-chain send, and geo-weekly-cron gains a checkpoint. Neither is in scope here.
